skill.name: starknet-wallet
skill.description: Manage Starknet wallet operations for agent workflows, including balances, token transfers, contract calls, session keys, and paymaster-based gasless transactions.
skill.summary: Guide Starknet wallet balances, transfers, contract calls, session keys, and gasless transaction patterns.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown backticks, TypeScript template literals, documented URLs, and static relative links. The meaningful risks are that the skill handles Starknet signing credentials and guides state-changing wallet operations that can move assets. No prompt injection attempts were found.

remediation.issue: Private key handling in examples and documentation
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a secure secret store, hardware-backed signer, or limited session key. Do not place long-lived private keys in shared .env files, prompts, logs, or repositories.

remediation.issue: State-changing wallet operations can move assets
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, dry-run summaries, recipient allowlists, spend limits, and fee review before transfers, invokes, swaps, or approvals.

remediation.issue: Third-party RPC and paymaster endpoints are part of the workflow
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that RPC and paymaster providers can observe transaction metadata. Allow users to configure trusted endpoints.

remediation.issue: Example scripts print wallet addresses and balances
remediation.suggestion: Avoid logging wallet details in shared terminals or CI logs. Redact addresses when full values are not required.

content.value_statement: Starknet wallet workflows require precise account, token, and RPC handling. This skill guides balance checks, transfers, contract calls, and session key patterns.
actual_capabilities: Check single token balances using Starknet RPC patterns.
Check multiple token balances with batch balance examples.
Prepare token transfers with optional paymaster gas handling.
Document contract read and write calls through MCP tool examples.
Explain session key policies for agent wallet autonomy.
limitations: Requires a configured Starknet RPC endpoint and wallet address.
State-changing transfers and invokes need signing credentials or MCP tools.
Does not audit smart contracts or verify recipient intent.
Examples depend on Starknet, starknet.js, and AVNU service availability.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Wallet Workflows
use_cases.description: Create balance, transfer, and contract call flows for a Starknet agent wallet.

use_cases.title: Monitor Token Balances
use_cases.description: Review ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT balances before running wallet operations.

use_cases.title: Design Session Key Policies
use_cases.description: Define spend limits, expiry rules, and allowed contract methods for agent autonomy.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Wallet Balance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Starknet wallet skill to check the ETH balance for this account address. Explain the token address, formatted amount, and raw amount.

prompt_templates.title: Review Batch Balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Check balances for ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT on this Starknet account. Summarize non-zero balances and mention the query method used.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Transfer Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a STRK transfer plan for this recipient and amount. Verify inputs, estimate fees, and ask for explicit confirmation before any state-changing action.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Session Key
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a session key policy for an agent that can transfer limited USDC only to approved addresses. Include spend caps, expiry, revocation, and monitoring rules.

output_examples.input: Check the STRK balance for my Starknet wallet.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the wallet address, token symbol, token contract, formatted balance, raw balance, and decimals used for formatting.

output_examples.input: Plan a gasless transfer of 25 USDC to an approved recipient.
output_examples.output: The response lists the recipient, token, amount, paymaster option, fee token, required checks, and a confirmation request before execution.

output_examples.input: Create a session key policy for a support agent wallet.
output_examples.output: The response proposes allowed contracts, allowed methods, per-transaction limits, total spend limits, expiry, and revocation steps.

best_practices: Require explicit user confirmation before every state-changing transaction.
Use least-privilege session keys with spend limits and expiry dates.
Keep private keys out of prompts, logs, repositories, and shared files.
anti_patterns: Do not store long-lived private keys in committed or shared environment files.
Do not approve unlimited spending for agent-controlled wallets.
Do not run mainnet transfers without recipient checks, fee review, and simulation.

faq.question: Does this skill create a wallet by itself?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples for wallet operations. Actual account creation depends on the configured Starknet tools and signer.

faq.question: Can it send tokens?
faq.answer: Yes, the skill documents token transfer workflows. Users should require explicit confirmation before any transfer is executed.

faq.question: Does it support gasless transactions?
faq.answer: Yes, it describes paymaster-based gas handling through AVNU and Starknet account abstraction patterns.

faq.question: What secrets are required?
faq.answer: State-changing operations usually require signing credentials. Use a secure secret store or limited session key when possible.

faq.question: Can it check several token balances at once?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes batch balance patterns for multiple token symbols or contract addresses.

faq.question: Is this a smart contract audit tool?
faq.answer: No. It supports wallet operations and contract interactions, but it does not audit contract safety.
